descriptionChirho: To make a loud, turbulent roaring sound, said of the sea, waters, or the tumult of nations and peoples.
To be inwardly agitated, disturbed, or restless, especially of the soul or heart in distress (as in Psalms 42-43).
To utter sounds of grief, distress, or lamentation, ranging from quiet moaning to howling and the growling of bears as a figure of mourning.
To be boisterous, loud, or clamorous, used of persons (especially the 'loud woman' of Proverbs) and noisy streets or places.
